name: Jusjab-Hesed
title: Solomon's District Administrator
summary: Jusjab-Hesed (Ben-Hesed) was one of King Solomon's twelve district administrators responsible for providing food for the king's household. He governed the district of Arubbót, which included Soko and all the land of Hefer. His role was vital to the administrative organization of the united kingdom under Solomon.

keyEvents.title: Appointed as District Administrator
keyEvents.description: Jusjab-Hesed was appointed by King Solomon as one of twelve district administrators responsible for supplying the royal household with food for one month each year.

keyEvents.title: Administration of the Arubbót District
keyEvents.description: He was in charge of Arubboth, including Socoh and all the land of Hepher, an important agricultural area in western Israel.

keyEvents.title: Part of Solomon's administrative system
keyEvents.description: Solomon's organization of Israel into twelve supply districts, with Jushab-Hesed as a key figure, ensured efficient management of the kingdom's resources.

keyEvents.title: Provision for the king's household
keyEvents.description: Each of the twelve governors, including Jushab-Hesed, provided food for King Solomon and his household one month each year, testifying to the wealth of the kingdom.
